angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 422,290 km at 128.50 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.7823 +/- 0.0111 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 128.50 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.607 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Lin et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1899 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...90L/abstract): 422,290 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.632 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Lin et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1899 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...90L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3926 +/- 45 K from Lin et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1899 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...90L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lin et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1899 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...90L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1899.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.672, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
